extracted.intended_audience: physician-scientist applicants to the NIH K99/R00 (early-career clinician-scientists) and peers advising them
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether a clinician with primarily clinical/translational experience, limited bench experience, and some prior publications/funding would meet the expectations for an NIH K99 (Pathway to Independence) award. The page is a forum post asking if a specific applicant profile is sufficient for K99 eligibility and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected lab research time (18 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The middle 18-months of fellowship is blocked out for lab research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: availability of contiguous protected research time during fellowship to conduct the K99/R00 transition-phase research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and relevance of mentorship/PI
rubrics_metrics.description: I will be working with a very well know PI who does mostly second generation whole genome sequencing of tumors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative point: having an established, relevant mentor and research environment is important for K99 applications; the post cites a well-known PI in a genomics-focused lab as a strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior bench research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: I have almost no bench research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit question: whether limited hands-on bench experience weakens eligibility/competitiveness for K99, which typically supports transition to independent basic/translational research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior grant/funding history
rubrics_metrics.description: I have applied in the past for a R21 (did not get funded) but received seed funding (20 K) from my institution as a Co-PI with others for work related to circulating tumor cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: prior experience applying for grants and having institutional/seed funding (even as co-PI) may support the application, though the post notes an unfunded R21 and modest seed funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record and types
rubrics_metrics.description: I have 15 publications (reviews, case reports etc) in peer-reviewed journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative point: number of publications is a factor, but the types (reviews, case reports vs original bench/translational research articles) may influence reviewers' assessment of research productivity and readiness for K99.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the proposed research (hypothesis-driven translational/basic science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose I write a strong hypothesis-driven translational/basic science grant application with the help of my mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: the scientific rigor and hypothesis-driven nature of the proposed research is central to K99 competitiveness; the poster asks whether a strong translational/basic science proposal can compensate for limited bench experience.
